common_distractors: the difference quotient of the function at the endpoints
the value of the integral without the division
the average of the endpoint values
division by the number of data points
common_givens: a model function in a context
a closed interval of the independent variable
archetypes.description: A function is given by a model formula or a graph, and the response computes its average value over a stated interval and reports it in context.
difficulty_variables: formula versus graph presentation
whether the interval starts at zero
whether an interpretation with units is demanded
whether the average value is compared with an average rate of change in a later part
expected_solution_path: write the definite integral of the function over the interval
divide by the length of the interval
evaluate with technology
report to three places after the decimal point with units
archetypes.invariant_structure: One function, one closed interval, one quotient: the definite integral of the function over the interval divided by the length of the interval, with the setup shown before the decimal.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of the calculator active free response question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Average value of a function over an interval
safe_variables: the letters used for the variables
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Two points: one for the correct integral together with evidence of division by the length of the interval, and one for the correct value reported to three decimal places; in 2025 unclear communication between the integral and the answer was treated as scratch work and both points were awarded (sg-25:3), while a 2023 response presenting the same kind of unlinked chain earned one of two points (sg-23:4).
typical_wording: find the average value of the modelled quantity over the stated time interval and show the setup for the calculations
using correct units, interpret the meaning of the average you found
wrong_approaches: averaging the two endpoint values
dividing by the upper limit alone

common_distractors: the value of the average rate of change reported as the answer
the average value of the function used in place of the average rate of change
archetypes.description: The response computes the average rate of change of a modelled quantity over an interval and solves for the time at which the derivative equals that value.
difficulty_variables: whether the interval starts where the function is zero, which makes several equivalent expressions acceptable
whether the derivative is supplied or must be computed
expected_solution_path: compute the average rate of change over the interval
set the given derivative equal to that value
solve numerically on the interval
report the input to three decimal places
archetypes.invariant_structure: A difference quotient of the modelling function over the interval, set equal to the given derivative, solved numerically for one input in the interval.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of the calculator active free response question.
archetypes.name: Instantaneous rate set equal to an average rate of change
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Two points: one for using the average rate of change, which several equivalent expressions earn, and one for the answer with the supporting equation; presenting the value of the average rate of change alone as the answer earns neither (sg-25:4).
typical_wording: find the time at which the instantaneous rate of change of the modelled quantity equals its average rate of change over the stated interval, and show the setup
wrong_approaches: reporting the average rate of change itself as the time

common_distractors: the displacement offered where total distance is asked
the integral of velocity without the initial position
the value of velocity at an endpoint
archetypes.description: A velocity function is given for a particle on a line, and the response produces displacement, total distance, or a position value from an initial condition.
difficulty_variables: whether velocity changes sign inside the interval
whether the question asks for displacement or total distance
whether an initial condition must be used
graph versus formula presentation
expected_solution_path: classify the requested quantity
write the matching definite integral
use the initial condition when a position value is requested
evaluate and report with units
archetypes.invariant_structure: One velocity function on a time interval; the requested quantity fixes the integrand as velocity, as the absolute value of velocity, or as velocity added to a known initial position.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Usually two or three parts of a multipart question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Rectilinear motion analysed with definite integrals
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no rectilinear part in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions; the planar analogue appears at 2024 Q2(b) and 2024 Q2(c)
safe_variables: the units of position and time
archetypes.scoring_pattern: The integral of speed earns a setup point and the decimal earns the answer point, the pattern the planar analogue uses at sg-24:6; a position value earns a point for the definite integral, a point for using the initial condition, and a point for the answer (sg-24:7).
typical_wording: find the total distance travelled by the particle over the stated time interval and show the setup
find the position of the particle at the later time
wrong_approaches: integrating velocity and taking the absolute value of the result
adding the absolute values of the endpoint velocities

asked_to_produce: an integral expression with the initial value
common_distractors: the value of the integral reported as the amount
the initial value subtracted rather than added
the rate evaluated at the endpoint
common_givens: a known value of the quantity at one time
archetypes.description: A rate of change is modelled on an interval and a value of the quantity is known at one time, and the response reports the quantity at another time.
difficulty_variables: whether the rate is given by a formula, a table, or a graph
whether the initial value is given directly or must be read
whether the integrand is antidifferentiable by hand
expected_solution_path: write the amount as the known value plus the definite integral of the rate
evaluate the integral
add the known value
report with units
archetypes.invariant_structure: A known value at one time plus the definite integral of the rate from that time to the requested time, evaluated numerically and reported in the units of the quantity.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart free response question.
archetypes.name: Amount at a later time from an initial amount and a rate
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Three points in the calculator active setting: the definite integral, the use of the initial condition, and the answer (sg-24:4, sg-24:7). In the no calculator setting the integrand and the antiderivative are separate points and the answer is a third (sg-25:14).
typical_wording: find the value of the modelled quantity at the later time and show the setup for the calculations
based on the model, how much of the quantity has accumulated by the end of the interval
wrong_approaches: reporting the net change as the amount
antidifferentiating and substituting only the upper limit

common_distractors: the sum of the two rates in place of the difference
the integral of the inflow alone
the difference taken in the wrong order
archetypes.description: Two rates act on the same quantity at once and the response works with their difference to describe the amount stored.
difficulty_variables: whether the two rates are both formulas or one is tabulated
whether the question asks for an amount, a net change, or a time of maximum
whether the interval is split where the net rate changes sign
expected_solution_path: write the net rate as inflow minus outflow
integrate the net rate over the interval
add the initial amount when an amount is requested
report with units
archetypes.invariant_structure: Two rate functions on a common interval; the net rate is their difference and every requested quantity is built from the integral of that difference added to a known amount.
archetypes.multipart_structure: Two or three parts of one multipart free response question.
archetypes.name: Accumulation with a rate in and a rate out
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no rate in and rate out part appears in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions
safe_variables: the names of the two processes
archetypes.scoring_pattern: The setup point requires the difference of the two rates inside one integral, and the answer point requires the value with the initial amount included; the Chief Reader records parenthesis loss when a given expression is substituted into an integrand as BC-ERR-99009.
typical_wording: the quantity enters at one modelled rate and leaves at another; find the amount present at the stated time and show the setup
wrong_approaches: integrating each rate and subtracting the wrong way round
dropping the parentheses around the outflow rate

asked_to_produce: an equation for the critical point
common_distractors: a first derivative test offered alone
the endpoint of the interval
the critical point of the rate rather than of the amount
common_givens: an amount function defined with a definite integral
archetypes.description: An amount function defined with an integral is given on a closed interval, and the response finds where it attains its maximum and justifies the claim globally.
difficulty_variables: whether the derivative must be assembled from a given rate and a subtracted term
whether the candidates test or a sign change argument is used
the number of candidates in the interval
expected_solution_path: differentiate the amount function
set the derivative equal to zero and solve numerically
evaluate the amount at the candidate and at both endpoints, or argue from a unique sign change
report the time
archetypes.invariant_structure: One amount function on a closed interval, one critical point found by setting its derivative equal to zero, and a justification that compares the candidate with both endpoints or argues from a unique sign change.
archetypes.multipart_structure: The closing part of the calculator active free response question.
archetypes.name: Time at which an accumulated amount is maximal
safe_variables: the form of the two competing terms
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Three points: considering the derivative equal to zero, a global justification, and the answer; a first or second derivative test presented alone does not earn the justification point but leaves the answer point available (sg-25:5).
typical_wording: at what time in the stated interval does the modelled amount attain its maximum value, and justify the answer
wrong_approaches: presenting a local argument for a global claim
omitting one endpoint from the candidates table

asked_to_produce: a sentence with quantity, interval, and units
common_distractors: the rate at an endpoint
the average value of the rate
the amount present rather than the change
archetypes.description: A definite integral of a contextual rate is displayed and the response states what it measures, over which interval, in which units.
difficulty_variables: whether the expression carries a factor that makes it an average
whether the integrand is a rate or a quantity
whether the interval is stated in the stem or only in the limits
expected_solution_path: identify the integrand as a rate
name the quantity accumulated
name the interval from the limits
attach the units
archetypes.invariant_structure: One integral expression and one sentence that names the accumulated quantity, the interval, and the units built as the rate units times the input units.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart question, often attached to a numerical approximation in the same part.
archetypes.name: Interpreting a definite integral of a rate in context
archetypes.scoring_pattern: One point, earned only when the quantity, the interval, and the units are all present; in 2023 the point required reference to the gallons pumped and to the two times bounding the interval (sg-23:2).
typical_wording: using correct units, interpret the meaning of the displayed definite integral in the context of the problem
wrong_approaches: naming the quantity without the interval
giving the units of the rate rather than of the accumulation

asked_to_produce: an antiderivative or a numerical value
common_distractors: the reversed difference
the integral of one function alone
the difference of the two areas taken with the wrong sign
common_givens: a figure with a shaded region
sometimes the value of one definite integral
archetypes.description: A shaded region bounded by two graphs is shown and the response sets up and evaluates the area integral in x.
difficulty_variables: whether the limits require a numerical solve
whether one of the two integrals is supplied as a number
whether an antiderivative is needed by hand
whether the region is bounded by a vertical line rather than an intersection
expected_solution_path: decide which curve is upper
write the integral of the difference with the correct limits
evaluate, using a supplied integral value where one is given
report the area
archetypes.invariant_structure: Two boundary curves, one interval, one integrand that is the upper curve minus the lower curve, and a nonnegative reported value.
archetypes.multipart_structure: The opening part of a multipart no calculator question, or one part of a calculator active question.
archetypes.name: Area of a region between two curves in x
safe_variables: the position of the region in the plane
archetypes.scoring_pattern: Three points in 2023: the integrand, an antiderivative of the explicitly given function, and the answer; a response writing the reversed difference and asserting it equals the positive area did not earn the answer point, while the same work stated correctly earned all three (sg-23:16, sg-23:17).
typical_wording: find the area of the shaded region enclosed by the graphs of the two functions
wrong_approaches: integrating the difference over an interval that extends past an intersection
reporting a negative value as an area

common_distractors: an integrand in x paired with a dy differential
limits taken as x values
the reversed difference
common_givens: curve equations in x or in y
archetypes.description: A region whose left and right boundaries are curves is presented, and the response integrates the difference of the curves with respect to y.
difficulty_variables: whether the curves must be inverted first
whether the region would need two integrals in x
whether limits are y values read from the figure
expected_solution_path: write both boundaries as functions of y
decide which is to the right
integrate the difference with respect to y over the y interval
report the area
archetypes.invariant_structure: Two boundary curves written as functions of y, one interval of y values, and an integrand that is the right curve minus the left curve.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Area of a region integrated with respect to y
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no area with respect to y appears in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions
archetypes.scoring_pattern: A setup point for the integrand and limits in y and an answer point for the value, following the area scoring pattern of 2023 (sg-23:16).
typical_wording: find the area of the region bounded by the two curves by integrating with respect to y
wrong_approaches: integrating the original functions of x between y limits

asked_to_produce: a sum of definite integrals or one absolute value integral
common_distractors: one integral of the difference across the whole interval
the sum of the signed contributions
only the larger lobe
archetypes.description: Two curves cross inside the interval, so the area is a sum of integrals or a single integral of an absolute value.
difficulty_variables: the number of interior crossings
whether the crossings are exact or decimal
whether the absolute value form is allowed by the calculator status
expected_solution_path: solve for every intersection in the interval
order the crossings
fix the order of subtraction on each piece
sum the integrals or integrate the absolute value
archetypes.invariant_structure: Two curves with at least one interior intersection; the area is additive over the subintervals and each contribution is nonnegative.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart question, or a single multiple choice item.
archetypes.name: Area of a region whose boundary curves cross
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no split region area appears in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions
archetypes.scoring_pattern: The setup point requires every piece of the region, so a single integral across a crossing loses it, and the answer point follows the setup, in the pattern the 2023 area part uses (sg-23:16).
typical_wording: find the total area of the region bounded by the two graphs over the stated interval
wrong_approaches: integrating a fixed difference across a crossing

common_distractors: an integrand carrying a factor of pi
the area of the base region
a semicircle area using the distance as the radius
common_givens: the shape of the cross sections
the axis they are perpendicular to
archetypes.description: A plane region is the base of a solid whose cross sections perpendicular to an axis are a named shape, and the response integrates the area of those sections.
difficulty_variables: the shape of the cross section
whether the distance is a side, a leg, a hypotenuse, or a diameter
whether the slicing axis is x or y
whether technology may evaluate the integral
expected_solution_path: write the distance between the boundary curves
substitute it into the area formula of the named shape
integrate over the spanning interval
report the volume
archetypes.invariant_structure: One base region, one axis of slicing, one named shape whose area formula is applied to the distance between the boundary curves, and one integral over the spanning interval.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart question that often opens with an area part on the same region.
archetypes.name: Volume of a solid with known cross sections
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no known cross section volume appears in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions
archetypes.scoring_pattern: A setup point for the integrand together with the limits and an answer point for the value; the Chief Reader records integrands taken from the wrong area or volume family as BC-ERR-99011.
typical_wording: the base of a solid is the given region and its cross sections perpendicular to the stated axis are the named shape; find the volume of the solid
wrong_approaches: using the full circle area for a semicircular section
squaring the boundary functions separately

asked_to_produce: an integrand with a squared radius
common_distractors: the radius left unsquared
the factor of pi omitted
the radius written without the shift when the axis is not a coordinate axis
archetypes.description: A region touching its axis of revolution is revolved and the response integrates pi times the square of the radius.
difficulty_variables: whether the axis is a coordinate axis or another line
whether the slicing variable is x or y
whether the answer is left as a multiple of pi
expected_solution_path: write the radius as a distance to the axis
square it and multiply by pi
integrate over the spanning interval
report the volume
archetypes.invariant_structure: One curve, one axis of revolution that the region meets, a radius equal to the distance from the curve to that axis, and a volume equal to pi times the integral of the square of that radius.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart question built on a region introduced earlier.
archetypes.name: Volume of a solid of revolution by the disc method
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no solid of revolution appears in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions
archetypes.scoring_pattern: A setup point for pi with the squared radius and the limits, and an answer point for the value; the Chief Reader records the wrong volume family as BC-ERR-99011.
typical_wording: the region is revolved about the stated line; find the volume of the solid generated
wrong_approaches: shifting the limits of integration along with the axis

asked_to_produce: an integrand with two squared radii
common_distractors: the square of the difference of the radii
the radii assigned by which curve is higher rather than which is farther
the shift omitted from both radii
common_givens: an axis of revolution the region does not meet
archetypes.description: A region separated from its axis of revolution is revolved and the response integrates pi times the difference of the squares of the two radii.
difficulty_variables: whether the axis is a coordinate axis or another line
whether the axis lies above or below the region, which can exchange the radii
whether the slicing variable is x or y
expected_solution_path: decide which curve is farther from the axis
write both radii as distances
square each radius and subtract
multiply by pi and integrate
report the volume
archetypes.invariant_structure: Two boundary curves, one axis of revolution the region does not meet, and an integrand equal to the square of the outer radius minus the square of the inner radius, both measured from the axis.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart question built on a region introduced earlier.
archetypes.name: Volume of a solid of revolution by the washer method
archetypes.official_examples_notes: no washer volume appears in the 2023 to 2025 BC free response questions
archetypes.scoring_pattern: A setup point for the two squared radii with pi and the limits, and an answer point for the value; a swapped pair of radii produces a negative value and loses the answer point.
typical_wording: the region between the two curves is revolved about the stated line; find the volume of the solid generated
wrong_approaches: squaring the difference of the two functions
reporting a negative volume from swapped radii

asked_to_produce: an integral expression, or a sentence naming arc length and the interval
common_distractors: the area under the curve
the total distance travelled by a particle on the x axis
the average value of the derivative
common_givens: a function, sometimes only through a table of its derivative
archetypes.description: A function is given on an interval and the response either writes and evaluates the arc length integral or identifies a displayed integral as an arc length.
difficulty_variables: whether the response must produce the integral or interpret a supplied one
whether the interval must be named explicitly
whether the integrand is evaluated numerically
expected_solution_path: differentiate the function
square the derivative and add one
take the square root and integrate over the interval
report the length, or name the length and its interval when interpreting
archetypes.invariant_structure: One differentiable function, one closed interval, and the integral of the square root of one plus the square of the derivative, read in either direction between expression and meaning.
archetypes.multipart_structure: One part of a multipart BC only no calculator question, or a calculator active setup and value part.
archetypes.name: Arc length of a curve given by a function
archetypes.scoring_pattern: In 2024 the identification was worth two points, one for naming the arc length of the function and one for naming the interval (sg-24:16); a numerical arc length part is scored as a setup point and an answer point.
typical_wording: what information does the displayed integral give about the graph of the function
find the length of the curve on the stated interval and show the setup
wrong_approaches: naming the arc length without naming the interval
omitting the square on the derivative
